export const meta = {
  name: 'workflow-ux-audit-design',
  description: 'Audit the Projects/workflow viewer UX through four lenses, draft three competing redesigns, judge them, synthesize one spec, and check it for gaps',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'four lenses over screenshots, code and live API payloads' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: 'three competing redesign proposals' },
    { title: 'Judge', detail: 'operator-fit and feasibility judges score all proposals' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'one merged spec with slices and acceptance criteria' },
    { title: 'Critic', detail: 'completeness check against every P1 finding; one revision if needed' },
  ],
}

const S = args.scratch
const CONTEXT = `
PRODUCT: MD Manager (repo /home/agentops/dev/md-manager) is a local web app. Its "Projects" section is a READ-ONLY viewer of agent workflow runs produced by the repo's Python controller (\`python -m workflow\`): each run is a LangGraph pipeline per feature — design challenge (print job) → launch_<lane> worker agent sessions (one per lane) → handoff/freeze → verify_<lane> (trusted verifier runs checks) → candidate (combined checks) → independent review (1+ reviewer agents, native or print transport) → approval → integrate. Runs are started, resumed, answered and approved ONLY from the CLI; the viewer never mutates.

THE USER'S COMPLAINT (verbatim): "Lets work on making the UX better for the workflow section. Its not good, i need to look around to understand whats where when it happened and overall is just bad."
The user operates runs daily, often watching a live run from a Mac browser while agents work on a VPS. Typical questions: What is happening right now / which step is active? Did it pass, and if not, why and what do I do next (which CLI command)? When did each step start/finish and how long did it take? What did the worker change, which checks ran, where are the screenshots/logs? What did the reviewers find? Is a worker waiting on a question?

MATERIAL (read it; do not guess):
- Screenshots of the CURRENT UI (live data): ${S}/shots/*.png. "-fold" = first 900px, "-full" = full page. Pages: 01 projects list, 02 project, 03 workflow run list, 04 run page (skeleton-001, failed at review), 05-08 node pages of skeleton-001 (challenge, launch_game [~20000px tall!], verify_game, review), 09-12 skeleton-fixes-001 (succeeded run) run/review/candidate/handoff, 13 a two-lane md-manager run, 14 the run's Assignment tab, and -mobile variants (390px) of 03/04/07. Use the Read tool on the PNGs (large ones are downscaled; the -fold images are sharp).
- Live API payloads: ${S}/api/*.json — <run>.detail.json (summary+definition+snapshot), <run>.events.json (the event timeline with occurred_at, node_id, status, message), <run>.inputs.json (pinned policy, lanes, checks, completion signals, questions, challenge, decisions), result_*.json (worker/candidate results: checks with started_at/finished_at, artifacts, changed files, screenshots) and reviews_*.json (review verdict, reviewers, findings). The live API is at http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/projects (read-only GETs are fine).
- Code: src/projects/*.tsx (ProjectsView.tsx levels, RunView.tsx run page, NodeDetail.tsx node inspector, ReviewDetail.tsx, WorkerInputs.tsx, Assignment.tsx, Challenge.tsx, CreatedFiles.tsx, WorkflowGraph.tsx, status.ts wording, panels.tsx), src/App.css (styles), src/App.tsx (app shell: header, Pi/Claude/Projects roots, Refresh button), contracts/projects/v1.ts (the API contract), server/projects.ts (how the server projects state; what data exists), tests/project-workflows/*.spec.ts (existing browser tests and data-testids they depend on).
- Prior design intent: docs/PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md, docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md, docs/PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md, docs/PRD_WORKER_LANES.md. Earlier slices deliberately added honesty wording ("a succeeded worker is not workflow completion", executor legends, read-only disclaimers). Respect the underlying truthfulness requirements but you may propose far more concise ways to convey them; the user now finds the page hard to use.
- Recent behaviour: run and list pages poll every 5 s (useResource pollToken / usePoll); the server projects live state from events.jsonl + run-state.json.

RULES: READ-ONLY. Do not edit repo files, do not commit, do not run Playwright or the test suites, do not restart servers on 3001/5173, do not touch ~/.local/state. You may write scratch files only under ${S}/work/. Be concrete: cite screenshot names, file:line, API fields. The Pi/Claude skills sections are out of scope.`

const AUDIT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string', description: 'short slug, unique within your lens' },
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['P1', 'P2', 'P3'], description: 'P1 = directly causes the user complaint (hunting around, cannot tell when/where/why)' },
      page: { type: 'string' },
      problem: { type: 'string' },
      evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'screenshot names, file:line, API fields' },
      user_impact: { type: 'string' },
      data_available: { type: 'string', description: 'which existing API fields could fix it, or "needs backend: ..."' },
      suggestion: { type: 'string' },
    }, required: ['id', 'severity', 'page', 'problem', 'evidence', 'user_impact', 'data_available', 'suggestion'] } },
    questions_by_page: { type: 'string', description: 'for each page level: the questions an operator arrives with, and whether the current page answers each within the first screen' },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['findings', 'questions_by_page', 'notes'],
}

const LENSES = [
  { key: 'orientation', prompt: `LENS: ORIENTATION & INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE ("what's where"). Walk every level (projects → project → workflow → run → node, plus the Assignment tab). For each: what is on the first screen, what is redundant (e.g. node list duplicating the graph, legends, disclaimers, metadata grids), what is missing, naming problems (e.g. every workflow is called "Feature implementation" — check workflow names vs feature names in the data), breadcrumb/route usefulness, where each kind of information lives (checks, logs, screenshots, changed files, findings, questions, commands to run) and how many clicks/scrolls it takes to reach it. Measure page heights from the screenshots. Identify the navigation model problems.` },
  { key: 'chronology', prompt: `LENS: TIME & CHRONOLOGY ("when it happened"). Inventory EVERY timestamp and duration the API exposes (events.occurred_at, summary created/updated, launch_requested_at/native_started_at, check started_at/finished_at, reviewer launched_at/accepted_at, reviewed_at, question asked_at/answered_at, completion signals, challenge attempts...). Then show what the UI renders today and where. Is there any run-level timeline? Are events only per node? Which nodes show "No events reference this node" although things happened (e.g. print-transport review, challenge)? Can the user tell how long each step took, when the run went idle, what happened most recently, retries/attempts over time? Are times absolute UTC only (the user is in a different timezone on a Mac)? Propose what a timeline/durations view could show purely from existing data, and list gaps that need backend events.` },
  { key: 'detail-density', prompt: `LENS: NODE DETAIL & EVIDENCE DENSITY. The node inspector (NodeDetail.tsx and children) produces pages of 3000–20000px (launch_game ~20000px). Break down section by section what each node kind shows (worker/launch, verification, candidate, review, challenge, handoff/prepare, integration) and in what order; measure which sections dominate the height (use the -full screenshots and the result/inputs payloads: e.g. every captured file inlined? every check log?). Decide for each section: essential-at-a-glance / on-demand / noise. Identify repeated information across node, run and Assignment tab. Consider how evidence (screenshots, logs, diffs, changed files, findings) should be progressively disclosed. Note mobile (390px) problems.` },
  { key: 'live-status', prompt: `LENS: LIVE STATUS & NEXT ACTION ("what is going on now, what do I do"). Using the three runs (one failed at review, one succeeded, one older two-lane run) and the server's projection rules (server/projects.ts projectSnapshot, status.ts wording), evaluate: can the user see at a glance which step is active, whether a worker is working/idle/blocked/waiting on a question, how long it has been running vs its deadline, why a run failed (e.g. skeleton-001's review blocked with a P1 — is that visible on the run page without clicking?), and what CLI command resolves the situation (retry/resume/answer/repair/accept-challenge — find them in workflow/*.py help text and README/RUNBOOK if present)? Does the auto-refresh (5 s poll) give any feedback (last updated / live indicator)? Are status colours and labels (Succeeded/Failed/Paused/Awaiting approval, attempt counters, executor legend) understandable? Is the runs list informative (duration, current step, verdict)?` },
]

phase('Audit')
const audits = (await parallel(LENSES.map(lens => () =>
  agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${lens.prompt}\n\nReturn findings ranked most severe first (aim for completeness within your lens, typically 8-20 findings).`,
    { label: `audit:${lens.key}`, phase: 'Audit', schema: AUDIT_SCHEMA })
    .then(r => r && { lens: lens.key, ...r })))).filter(Boolean)
log(`Audit: ${audits.map(a => `${a.lens} ${a.findings.length}`).join(', ')} findings`)
const auditText = JSON.stringify(audits, null, 1)

const PROPOSAL_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    name: { type: 'string' },
    thesis: { type: 'string', description: 'the organising idea in 2-4 sentences' },
    information_architecture: { type: 'string', description: 'markdown: levels/routes, what each page answers first, what moves where, what is removed or merged' },
    wireframes: { type: 'string', description: 'markdown with ASCII wireframes for: runs list, run page (desktop, first screen), node inspector for a worker lane, for review, and the run page at 390px' },
    timeline: { type: 'string', description: 'how chronology is shown (run timeline, durations, relative+local times, attempts), built from which fields' },
    live_and_next_action: { type: 'string', description: 'how current step, waiting states, failure reason and the next CLI command are surfaced' },
    evidence_disclosure: { type: 'string', description: 'how checks, logs, screenshots, changed files, findings, inputs are progressively disclosed' },
    removed_or_demoted: { type: 'string' },
    data_needs: { type: 'string', description: 'existing API fields used; any backend/contract additions (keep minimal, justify each)' },
    implementation: { type: 'string', description: 'files/components to add/change, rough size, and a slice order' },
    test_impact: { type: 'string', description: 'which existing Playwright specs/testids break and how to migrate; new tests' },
    risks: { type: 'string' },
    addresses_findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'audit finding ids (lens:id) this proposal fixes' },
  },
  required: ['name', 'thesis', 'information_architecture', 'wireframes', 'timeline', 'live_and_next_action', 'evidence_disclosure', 'removed_or_demoted', 'data_needs', 'implementation', 'test_impact', 'risks', 'addresses_findings'],
}

const ANGLES = [
  { key: 'timeline-first', prompt: 'ANGLE: TIMELINE-FIRST. The run page is organised around chronology: a run timeline (what happened when, how long each step took, what is happening now) is the primary surface; the graph becomes a compact progress strip; node details open from timeline entries.' },
  { key: 'triage-first', prompt: 'ANGLE: TRIAGE/STATUS-FIRST. The run page leads with an answer: a status headline (state, current step, elapsed vs deadline, why it stopped, the exact next CLI command), then per-lane cards (worker state, checks, questions, verdict), with deeper evidence one click away. The runs list becomes a dashboard of runs with current step/verdict/duration.' },
  { key: 'graph-inspector', prompt: 'ANGLE: SPLIT-PANE GRAPH + INSPECTOR. A full-width, always-visible pipeline (never clipped) with a persistent side/bottom inspector; each node inspector uses tabs (Summary / Timeline / Evidence / Inputs) so no node page is ever longer than ~2 screens; the Assignment tab content is folded into the relevant node tabs.' },
]

phase('Design')
const proposals = (await parallel(ANGLES.map(angle => () =>
  agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are a senior product designer + frontend engineer. Below are the audit findings from four lenses (JSON). Design a redesign of the Projects/workflow viewer.\n\n${angle.prompt}\n\nYour proposal must: fix every P1 finding you can, stay a read-only viewer, prefer existing API data (propose backend additions only where essential and small), keep accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, reduced motion) and the truthful-status requirements (expressed concisely), work at 390px, and be implementable incrementally in this codebase (React + TS, plain CSS in src/App.css, no new heavy dependencies). Read the code you need to be concrete about components and testids.\n\nAUDIT FINDINGS:\n${auditText}`,
    { label: `design:${angle.key}`, phase: 'Design', schema: PROPOSAL_SCHEMA })
    .then(r => r && { angle: angle.key, ...r })))).filter(Boolean)
const proposalText = JSON.stringify(proposals, null, 1)

const JUDGE_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    scores: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      angle: { type: 'string' },
      score: { type: 'number', description: '0-10' },
      strengths: { type: 'string' },
      weaknesses: { type: 'string' },
    }, required: ['angle', 'score', 'strengths', 'weaknesses'] } },
    winner: { type: 'string' },
    grafts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'specific ideas from any proposal the final design must include' },
    must_avoid: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['scores', 'winner', 'grafts', 'must_avoid'],
}
const JUDGES = [
  { key: 'operator', prompt: 'JUDGE LENS: THE OPERATOR. Score each proposal by how fast the user answers their real questions (what is happening now, why did it fail and what command next, when did each step happen and how long, where is the evidence, what did reviewers find, is a worker waiting on a question) on desktop and on a phone, and how completely it removes the "I need to look around" feeling. Walk through the three concrete runs in the API payloads against each proposal\'s wireframes.' },
  { key: 'feasibility', prompt: 'JUDGE LENS: FEASIBILITY & RISK. Score each proposal on: implementable with existing data (verify claimed API fields exist in contracts/projects/v1.ts and the payloads), size of backend/contract changes, test churn in tests/project-workflows (count affected testids/specs), accessibility (keyboard/screen reader for timeline/graph/tabs), performance with 5 s polling, mobile, and incremental delivery (can it ship in slices without a broken intermediate state).' },
]
phase('Judge')
const verdicts = (await parallel(JUDGES.map(judge => () =>
  agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${judge.prompt}\n\nAUDIT FINDINGS:\n${auditText}\n\nPROPOSALS:\n${proposalText}`,
    { label: `judge:${judge.key}`, phase: 'Judge', schema: JUDGE_SCHEMA })
    .then(r => r && { judge: judge.key, ...r })))).filter(Boolean)
log(`Judges: ${verdicts.map(v => `${v.judge} → ${v.winner}`).join('; ')}`)

const SPEC_PATH = `${S}/work/SPEC.md`
const synthPrompt = (extra) => `${CONTEXT}\n\nSynthesize the FINAL redesign spec for the Projects/workflow viewer from the audit, the three proposals and the two judges' verdicts. Start from the judges' winner(s), graft every listed graft that fits, honour every must_avoid. Write it as a PRD in the style of the repo's docs/PRD_*.md (read one or two for tone/structure) to ${SPEC_PATH} (create ${S}/work/ if needed). Required sections: 1 Problem (tie to the user's complaint and the P1 findings), 2 Goals / non-goals, 3 Information architecture, 4 Page designs with ASCII wireframes (runs list, run page first screen desktop + 390px, node inspector for worker lane, verification/candidate, review, challenge, handoff/integration), 5 Timeline & time display rules (local vs UTC, relative, durations, attempts), 6 Live state & next action (including the exact CLI command table per situation, verified against workflow/*.py and README), 7 Evidence disclosure rules, 8 Copy/wording (concise truthful status language replacing the current disclaimers), 9 Data: existing fields used per element + any backend/contract additions with justification, 10 Accessibility & mobile, 11 Implementation slices (ordered, each shippable, files touched, size, and which can run in parallel without file conflicts), 12 Test plan (new specs, testids, migration of existing specs, red/green expectations), 13 Open questions for the user (at most 5, each with a recommended default). Also append an appendix mapping EVERY audit finding id (lens:id) to the spec section that addresses it or to "won't fix: reason".${extra}\n\nAUDIT:\n${auditText}\n\nPROPOSALS:\n${proposalText}\n\nVERDICTS:\n${JSON.stringify(verdicts, null, 1)}\n\nReturn a short summary (<= 25 lines) of the design and the slice list.`

phase('Synthesize')
let summary = await agent(synthPrompt(''), { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize' })

const CRITIC_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    gaps: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      finding_or_topic: { type: 'string' }, problem: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' },
    }, required: ['finding_or_topic', 'problem', 'fix'] } },
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['complete', 'needs_revision'] },
  },
  required: ['gaps', 'verdict'],
}
phase('Critic')
const critique = await agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are the completeness critic. Read the spec at ${SPEC_PATH}. Check: (1) every P1 audit finding is genuinely addressed (not just mapped in the appendix); (2) every claimed API field exists (check contracts/projects/v1.ts and the payloads); (3) the CLI commands in the next-action table exist with those arguments (check workflow/pipeline.py argparse, workflow/__main__.py, README.md); (4) slices are each shippable and their parallel groups really touch disjoint files; (5) the wireframes answer the user's complaint on the first screen of the run page; (6) nothing makes the viewer mutate state. Report only real gaps.\n\nAUDIT:\n${auditText}`,
  { label: 'critic', phase: 'Critic', schema: CRITIC_SCHEMA })
if (critique && critique.verdict === 'needs_revision' && critique.gaps.length) {
  log(`Critic found ${critique.gaps.length} gaps; revising once`)
  summary = await agent(synthPrompt(`\n\nREVISION: the spec already exists at ${SPEC_PATH}; revise it in place to close these critic gaps:\n${JSON.stringify(critique.gaps, null, 1)}`),
    { label: 'revise', phase: 'Critic' })
}
return { spec: SPEC_PATH, summary, verdicts, critique, audit_counts: audits.map(a => ({ lens: a.lens, p1: a.findings.filter(f => f.severity === 'P1').length, total: a.findings.length })), proposals: proposals.map(p => ({ angle: p.angle, name: p.name, thesis: p.thesis })) }

result.summary:
Revised `SPEC.md` in place to close all 12 critic gaps, after checking each claim against the code (every one held). One edit goes past the critic's list: a run where a repair was applied but not yet continued now also gets its next step (`automatic --live` or `retry`), because the repair's own event message says so (repair.py:445). No repo files, tests or servers were touched.

**Design:**
- **Base:** the timeline-first proposal. Each run page opens with a "Now" banner (where the run stopped, why, since when, and the CLI command to type next). Below it are the fitted SVG graph and a Steps table with start, duration and attempt markers per step. The Activity list follows directly, and it shows the controller events the viewer hides today. Node pages get a sticky step strip, a header with verdict and timing, and a section index instead of one long column.
- **Next-step rules:** now 13 situations.
  - Rule 5 covers interruptions recorded on the review or freeze node itself, a dead controller, and the repair-continuation case above.
  - The new rule 6 covers runs the controller blocked before freeze. Its next step is a new run, because `repair` refuses these runs.
  - A paused run is never labelled "Failed".
  - `answer` shows the `--no-herdr` form for plain SSH shells.
  - The review-blocked fix is three steps: `init`, fill in and commit, `launch`.
  - `status` is described as changing no run progress (it refreshes report.html).
- **Server additions:**
  - Controller rows that have no node now keep their status.
  - A worker or reviewer that needs attention in its pane gets the same markers as a waiting question.
  - A new `activity.controller` field checks the logged PID's command line and start time in `/proc`, so a reused PID can never read as "running". It reports "unknown" off Linux.
  - Serving the run directory is now a top-level `viewer` key, because a per-workflow key would be dropped the next time that feature launches.
- **First screen:** the Projects header becomes one row and the tabs sit above the graph. The measured budget puts the failing step's row inside 1440×900 for runs with up to 2 lanes; with 3 or more lanes it can fall below the fold, and the goal now says so.

**Slices** (at most two at once; each parallel pair edits no common file):

| Step | Slices |
|---|---|
| 1 | S1 time, freshness and test plumbing ∥ S2 pure model |
| 2 | S3 run page ∥ S5 backend (server and contracts only) |
| 3 | S4-core: node shell, NodeDetail split per node kind, attempts route |
| 4 | S4a verify/candidate ∥ S4b launch |
| 5 | S4c review/challenge/controller ∥ S6 lists and client use of the new server fields |
| 6 | S7 depth |

Only S1 edits `package.json` (the unit-test script becomes a glob). Each slice has its own fixture module and spec file, and every browser scenario belongs to exactly one slice that does not depend on a later one. The test migrations are corrected, including the two `projects.spec.ts` assertions that would have broken (`:142`, `:149`).

**File:** /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/541817b2-200f-49c5-b924-e4e11cf0112a/scratchpad/ux/work/SPEC.md (1,215 lines)

scores.strengths:
The run page answers the user's actual complaint ("what's where, when it happened") with the fewest moving parts: Now banner, then a fitted Steps strip, then a per-try timeline, all on the first screen.

**skeleton-001**
- The banner names Independent review, general's P1 and MatchRoom.ts:44–50.
- The timeline shows the rows that are invisible today:
  - challenge tries 1–3, including the KeyboardInterrupt
  - worker 28m21s from the receipts
  - verify tries 1 and 2 failing
  - the #19 diagnosis row
  - a 5m37s operator gap
  - Repair 1
  - try 3 passing
  - an inferred review ≈2m10s
- These are the node_id-null events #19 and #21, which no page renders today.

**skeleton-fixes-001**
- The banner shows the integrated commit ee74298 (not pushed), 31m50s, and the review approved with 2 open P2.
- The timeline shows the challenge pause and the operator's resume.

**guardrails**
- Two parallel lane bars.
- The controller outages between 19:33 and 20:04 are classified as gaps.

**Structure**
- One element carries both the graph and the node list. This removes the clipped 1,680px SVG and the empty left third, and keeps the testids `workflow-graph` and `run-node-list`.
- Node view is full width, with a sticky strip and prev/next.
  - A try strip links `/attempts/<k>`, using the already-served `results/game/1` and `results/game/2`.
  - A section index with counts, rather than tabs, keeps Ctrl-F working and does not hide evidence.
  - The files list is taken from the worker's own freeze, with repair badges.
  - Gate reasons are mapped onto exit-0 checks.
- Mobile: tapping a step opens the node view and focuses its heading.

**Honesty and risk**
- Inferred values show ≈ and their source.
- When nothing matches, it says "No known next step matched" rather than guessing.
- It has the smallest test churn of the three (about 15 assertions), with a clear slice order (S1 time/freshness, S3 run page).
scores.weaknesses:
**guardrails-001:** the banner gets no command. `repair` is mapped only from a node-less 'failed identically' diagnosis event, and guardrails has none: its candidate simply failed twice with the same message (#28, #31). The RUNBOOK (line 298) names this exact run as the repair case, so the banner falls back to "No known next step matched".

**skeleton-001, review-blocked command:** `launch <new-feature> --automatic --live` omits the `--repo ~/dev/project-B` a non-md-manager target needs, and uses bare `python` instead of the RUNBOOK's `"$PY"` / `.venv/bin/python` run from the tool checkout.

**Live pill:** the wireframe shows "Finished · not polling" on failed skeleton-001. The code (ProjectsView.tsx) keeps polling failed runs, and a failed run can still be repaired and resumed.

**Mapping rules:** "a controller [Errno …]" is not scoped to the focus node's latest events. On guardrails it could match the four stale Errno failures (19:33–20:03).

**Multi-lane runs:** there is no per-lane summary. The fact that lane ui failed while lane controller passed shows up only in the candidate row and the banner.

**Gaps vs. worker span:** the "a working worker is a span, not a gap" rule conflicts with the claimed guardrails controller-down gaps, which fall inside the worker span.

**Background tab:** nothing like a `document.title` flag signals a waiting question on a background Mac tab.

**Fold:** at 1440×900 the failing review row sits below the fold; only the banner covers it.

scores.strengths:
It has the most complete first screen.
- The Now banner comes first, and the classifier covers the guardrails case correctly. Rule 5 treats "two consecutive failed events or lane errors with the same reason" as an identical failure, so guardrails gets `repair <run> ui --workspace`, then `automatic --live`, with the reason "lane ui: Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown".
- Lane cards give a per-lane view:
  - worker 28m, 0 questions
  - verify try 3 of 3, 2 failed tries, repair 1
  - candidate 5/5
  - findings 1 P1 / 3 P2
  - a review card showing "coverage superseded"
  These are exactly what a two-lane run needs.
- Steps rows pack each node's attempt story into one line ("Verify game 09:19 10m02s ✗✗⚒█ try 3 of 3 · repair 1").
- `triage.ts` is shared with the server to fill `RunSummary.glance`, so the dashboard headline matches the run page by construction.
- A `document.title` ⚑ prefix flags a waiting question or approval, which suits a Mac background tab.
- Questions is the default tab while a question waits.
- `run_dir` is home-relative, and null outside $HOME and in the test temp roots.
- Node tabs are routed, carry counts, and pick a default by situation.
scores.weaknesses:
**Wrong next step for skeleton-001.** The review-blocked command is `launch skeleton --run-id skeleton-002 --automatic --live`. That relaunches the original walking-skeleton feature, not the fixes. It also has no `--repo ~/dev/project-B`, so from the tool checkout it would target md-manager. It even contradicts its own caption "as skeleton-fixes-001 did", which was a new feature.

**Stale-event misclassification.** Rule 4 (`interrupted|exit 75|Errno`) is checked before the identical-failure rule and is not limited to the latest events. Guardrails' stale [Errno 2] and [Errno 8] events could classify it as "Claude Code unavailable".

**The pipeline appears three times on the overview:** the fitted SVG graph, the lane cards and the Steps list. This brings back the audit's "same graph as text" duplication and crowds the 900px fold.

**Chronology is behind a toggle.** Per-attempt history, node-less diagnosis and repair rows, and gaps are all in the Log view, not the default.

**Tabs hide evidence.** Routed tabs on every node break Ctrl-F across a node, and Files and Checks sit behind them.

**Live pill wrong on failed runs.** The wireframe also shows "Finished · not polling" for failed skeleton-001.

**Other issues:**
- About 25 assertions change.
- The graph fits only by shrinking to 136px nodes at a 0.83 scale.

scores.strengths:
Its concept suits "what's where" best: the same four tabs (Summary, Timeline, Evidence, Inputs) apply to the run and to every node. That gives the operator one map to learn.

**Next steps and live status**

must_avoid: **Unprescribed commands.** Never offer a concrete command the RUNBOOK does not prescribe for the situation. Examples: `launch skeleton --run-id skeleton-002` to 'fix' review findings; `git push` as a workflow next step; a command without `--repo` for another repository. When no rule matches, say 'No known next step matched' and link the RUNBOOK section.

**Stale classification.** Never classify a run from events other than the focus node's latest state. A stale `[Errno 2]` from an hour earlier must not turn a blocked-identical run into 'Claude Code unavailable'.
**Wrong live label.** Never show 'Finished · not polling' on a failed or paused run. Those can still be repaired or resumed, and the viewer keeps polling them.

**Split evidence.** Never split one node kind's primary evidence across two tabs (checks in both Summary and Evidence). Never hide the node's main evidence where Ctrl-F cannot reach it without a count on the index.
**Unmarked inference.** Never show an inferred time without '≈' and its source. Never invent start times for print-transport reviews, approvals or completion signals: say 'not recorded'.

**Wrong 'last activity'.** Never use `updated_at` or 'sequence N' as last activity or finish time. Never treat 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID' rows as a node running again (guardrails launch_controller #24/#29/#32).
**Misattributed files.** Never credit an operator repair's files to the worker: the launch node's file list comes from `results/<lane>/1`, with repair badges on later changes.
**File list rendering.** Never auto-fetch or auto-render Markdown files, and never render one panel per file with empty 'No review finding names this file' text.
**Exposed paths.** Never expose absolute run directories by default. `run_dir` stays opt-in and home-relative, and `redactPaths` stays the default.
**Commands in buttons.** Never put commands or file paths inside button text, which would trip `expectNoExecutionControls`. The viewer must stay strictly read-only.

**Big-bang rewrite.** Never land this as one rewrite that removes the Assignment tab and moves about 100 assertions at once. Ship the slices in order (time and freshness, then the run page, then the node view, then lists and backend), each with its own test migrations.

**Dropped honesty wording.** Never remove the honesty requirements outright. 'Session ended its turn, not workflow completion', 'as signalled by the session, not verified' and 'this viewer never changes a run' each appear once, compactly.

gaps.problem: Section 6.2 rule 5 only matches run-level RESUME_NOTE/UNAVAILABLE_NOTE rows. An interruption during the review wait or the freeze is recorded on the node itself: runtime.event("review", "interrupted", REVIEW_RESUME_NOTE) at automatic.py:624/738/804/811, and runtime.event("freeze", "interrupted", FREEZE_RESUME_NOTE) at :1314. The logged PID belongs to the automatic-step child (automatic.py:1244), whose argv is `python -m workflow automatic-step <run dir> --live` (automatic.py:1103), on the same host and user as the server.

Have S4-core split NodeDetail into per-kind section files (VerifySections, WorkerSections, ReviewSections, ControllerSections) with their own CSS, add RunView/ProjectsView to S4-core, and assign each fixture addition to one slice in separate fixture modules. gaps.finding_or_topic: Slices: tests that depend on later slices
gaps.problem: S1's time-local-utc asserts that 'the toggle switches the Steps header to UTC', but 5.3 places the toggle in the Steps header, which arrives in S3. S3's run-steps-timeline asserts that 'an Activity attempt link opens /nodes/<n>/attempts/<k>', but that route is added in S4-core; today parseProjectsPathname rejects trailing segments (routes.ts). S4's node-attempts needs both S4-core (route) and S4a (check-rejected rows). As written, S1 and S3 cannot go green alone.
gaps.fix: Put the S1 toggle on the run header (or move that assertion to S3). Add the attempts route to S3, or move the Activity-link assertion to S4-core. Assign each S4 scenario to exactly one sub-slice.

gaps.finding_or_topic: B3 opt-in run_dir (the copy-paste-ready commands for no-next-action)
gaps.problem: The 'to verify in S5' question can be answered now, and the answer is no. On re-registration, registry.py:184-190 rebuilds the workflow item from the fresh launch entry, keeping only `definition`, and the `existing == workflow` check then fails. Any extra key such as expose_run_dir is therefore dropped the next time that feature launches. Every new feature is appended without it (registry.py:191), so Open question 2's per-project default ('project-B and md-manager') cannot be expressed as a per-workflow flag. projectsConfig's workflowSchema is strict (projectsConfig.ts:37), so adding the key before S5 breaks config loading.

gaps.problem: projects.spec.ts:149 finds the definition graph with getByRole('group', {name: 'Current definition graph of …'}) on a workflow with 5 runs. Section 4.1 moves that graph into a <details> that stays closed while runs exist, and role queries skip hidden content, so this assertion fails in S6. It is not migrated (only :277, the empty workflow, stays open). projects.spec.ts:142 counts `run-list li` (5), while 4.1 says each row is one <a>. The S3 migration cites projects.spec.ts:308-310 for graphNode on node URLs; those assertions are at :317-319.

gaps.finding_or_topic: Next-step commands (6.2): accurate but incomplete for real use
gaps.problem: (a) Rule 1: `answer "$RUN" <lane> "<text>"` delivers only from a Herdr pane that shows the lane's attach. From a plain SSH shell, which is how the user works from the Mac, it records the answer, restarts the deadline and exits 1; the worker never receives it (RUNBOOK:56). The --no-herdr variant (guardrails.py:1001) is not shown. (b) Rule 8: the `launch <fixes-feature> --repo …` template fails unless features/<fixes-feature>/ exists, because launch refuses unknown features. The `init <fixes-feature> --repo <target>` step (scaffold.py:103-104) and the grill/commit step are missing. (c) Rule 12 calls `status "$RUN"` read-only, but it refreshes report.html in the run directory (RUNBOOK:272).
gaps.fix: Show the --no-herdr form and the one-line delivery caveat in the question block. Make rule 8 a three-step template: init, fill/grill and commit, launch. Describe `status` as 'reports state; changes no run progress'.

gaps.finding_or_topic: detail-density:gate-reason-not-on-check (P1): reasons without a check id
gaps.problem: Sections 4.6 and 7 key gate reasons by their `<check id>:` prefix. Real results also carry unprefixed reasons. workflow-guardrails-001 results/controller/1 has error.message 'Executed check failed: <path> -m workflow.run_tests; workflow-unit: …'. The path is redacted in the message but not in checks[].command, so neither a prefix nor a command match finds the check, and the spec does not say where such a reason goes.
gaps.fix: Specify that unkeyed segments are listed as gate-level reasons. Optionally match them by the command tail after '<path>' when exactly one check matches. Add controller/1 as a gateReasonsByCheck unit case.

gaps.problem: Section 4.7 sets the native reviewer deadline as `launch_requested_at + review_timeout_seconds`, but reviewerEntrySchema has only launched_at and accepted_at (contracts/projects/v1.ts:94). Section 5.2 rule 9 already uses launched_at. Section 4.1 says the pre-B2 list line 'Failed · 09:32 · 2 h ago · 52m51s' is built from created_at/updated_at. For skeleton-001, updated_at is 09:36:07 (server/projects.ts:936), which yields 09:36 and 56m27s: the misleading value that chronology:last-activity-misleading (P1) is about.
gaps.fix: Use reviewers[].launched_at in 4.7. For the pre-B2 fallback, either fetch the events of terminal latest runs once (they no longer change) to get the real end, or label the time 'updated 09:36' without a finish or duration claim until B2 supplies finished_at.

proposals.name: Run Story: a timeline-first workflow viewer
proposals.thesis:
A run happens in time, so the run page shows it in time order. The first screen answers three things at a glance:
1. A **Now banner**: where the run is or where it stopped, why, since when, and the CLI command to run next.
2. A **Steps strip**: the pinned graph as status chips with durations. It fits the page width, so there is no inner horizontal scroll.
3. A **Run timeline**: every step attempt, retry, repair, controller restart, question and idle gap, with local times and durations. This includes the events with no node (node_id null) that the viewer hides today.

Each timeline row opens a full-width node view. The view starts with the node's own verdict, timing and tries. Its evidence sits behind a section index with counts (Checks 5 · Screenshots 2 · Files 77 · Findings 4 …), instead of one column up to 20,000px tall.

Almost everything comes from data the run page already loads (events, snapshot, inputs, review) through one pure `buildTimeline()`. Three small server additions add status to the list pages, make run paths copyable, and fix how events are projected.

proposals.name: Answer-first run triage
proposals.thesis: Every Projects page should answer the operator's question in its top block, before it shows any evidence. A run page opens with a "Now" banner computed from existing data: the step where the run is or stopped, why in one line, when (local time plus how long ago), and the exact CLI command to run next with a Copy button. Below it come one card per lane (worker, verify, candidate, findings), then a step timeline with durations, which also serves as the node list. Deeper evidence (checks, logs, screenshots, files, findings, task) sits one click away in URL-addressable node tabs. One pure module, contracts/projects/triage.ts, does the classification and timing. The browser uses it first. The server reuses it later to give run lists the same headline, so the runs list becomes a dashboard sorted by what needs the operator.

proposals.name: Pinned Pipeline + Tabbed Inspector
proposals.thesis: Every run page has two panes. The first is a pipeline band that is always on screen, fits the page width, and is also the step list. The second is an inspector below it that answers questions in the same order everywhere: Summary (what happened, why, what do I type next), Timeline (when and how long), Evidence (proof), Inputs (what was asked). The run itself is the default subject; a step replaces it when selected. Above both sits a run header whose "Now" line names the active or failed step, its reason and the next CLI command before anything else. Each piece of evidence has exactly one home; every other page shows a one-line link to it. The pipeline never clips, and a node inspector is at most about two screens because long lists live in collapsed, filterable tables in the Evidence tab.
